title: Open root-product chart for an admissible Chevalley representation
statement:
Let $V$ be a finite-dimensional rational vector space and $R\subset V\setminus\{0\}$ a reduced crystallographic root system spanning $V$, with coroot functionals $\bar c_\alpha$ and weight lattice $P=\{v\in V:\bar c_\alpha(v)\in\mathbf Z\text{ for every }\alpha\in R\}$ in the conventions of [lem-sfb-root-datum-lattice-embedding]. Let $\mathfrak g,\mathfrak h,h_\delta,e_\alpha,\rho,W,\Omega,\Lambda$ satisfy the Chevalley-basis and faithful-representation conditions of [lem-sfb-chevalley-admissible-representation]: $\mathfrak g$ is split semisimple over $\mathbf Q$, $\rho$ is faithful on finite-dimensional $W$, the nonzero weight spaces $W_\lambda$ have weights $\Omega\subset P$ with $\mathbf Z\Omega=P$, and the full lattice $\Lambda=\bigoplus_{\lambda\in\Omega}(\Lambda\cap W_\lambda)$ is stable under every $D_{\alpha,m}=\rho(e_\alpha)^m/m!$, with $\rho(e_\alpha)$ nilpotent. Fix a simple-root base $\Delta$, meaning a subset $\Delta\subseteq R$ which is a basis of $V$ such that every root has integral coordinates in $\Delta$ all nonnegative or all nonpositive. Let $F$ be an algebraically closed field [def-weil-field, def-weil-algebraic-closure], $W_F=\Lambda\otimes_{\mathbf Z}F$, and $T=D_F(P)=\operatorname{Spec}F[P]$, where $F[P]$ has basis $e^\lambda$, multiplication $e^\lambda e^\mu=e^{\lambda+\mu}$, comultiplication $e^\lambda\mapsto e^\lambda\otimes e^\lambda$, counit $e^\lambda\mapsto1$, and antipode $e^\lambda\mapsto e^{-\lambda}$. Embed $T$ in $\operatorname{GL}(W_F)$ by its weight characters on the summands $(\Lambda\cap W_\lambda)\otimes F$. Define the finite polynomial matrices $x_\alpha(a)=\sum_{m\geq0}(D_{\alpha,m}\otimes1)a^m$ for every commutative $F$-algebra. Group schemes and closed subgroups have the meanings of [def-sc-group-scheme, def-sc-group-scheme-subgroup], and $\mathbf G_a,\mathbf G_m$ those of [def-sc-gm-ga]. Let $K\subseteq\operatorname{GL}(W_F)$ be the smallest closed subgroup containing $T$ and the images of all $x_\alpha$. Put $R^+=R\cap\sum_{\delta\in\Delta}\mathbf Z_{\geq0}\delta$, $N=|R^+|$, and enumerate $R^+$ by any total order refining nondecreasing height (height is the sum of the simple-root coefficients). Using that order for each product, the multiplication morphism
$$\mathbf A_F^N\times_F T\times_F\mathbf A_F^N\longrightarrow K,\qquad ((a_\beta),t,(b_\beta))\longmapsto\left(\prod_{\beta\in R^+}x_{-\beta}(a_\beta)\right)t\left(\prod_{\beta\in R^+}x_\beta(b_\beta)\right)$$
is an open immersion [def-weil-open-immersion] whose image contains the identity. It is equivariant for conjugation by $T$: the negative coordinates have characters $-\beta$, the positive coordinates have characters $\beta$, and $T$ acts trivially on the middle factor. In particular its differential identifies the tangent representation at the identity with
$$\operatorname{Lie}(K)=\operatorname{Lie}(T)\oplus\bigoplus_{\beta\in R}F\,d x_\beta(1),$$
where the displayed root vectors are nonzero and have the distinct torus characters $\beta$. Tangent spaces and their differentials are at the identity; the $1$ in $d x_\beta(1)$ is the unit vector in $T_0\mathbf G_a=F$. This assertion assumes no reductivity of $K$ and makes no identification with the reduction of a chosen integral Lie-algebra form. For $R=\varnothing$ the morphism is the identity of $T=1$.

source.place: Section 23h, Theorem 23.72 proof, pp.510-511: omitted details needed to use the weight-character torus rather than the full diagonal torus. The open-cell strengthening is an agent-stated construction lemma.

proof.text: The representation conditions give $D_{\alpha,i}D_{\alpha,j}=\binom{i+j}{i}D_{\alpha,i+j}$ on the torsion-free lattice, since this equality holds over $\mathbf Q$. Coefficient comparison therefore proves $x_\alpha(a)x_\alpha(b)=x_\alpha(a+b)$ and $x_\alpha(a)^{-1}=x_\alpha(-a)$ over every test algebra. The bracket $[h,e_\alpha]=\alpha(h)e_\alpha$ gives $D_{\alpha,m}(W_\lambda)\subseteq W_{\lambda+m\alpha}$, so $t x_\alpha(a)t^{-1}=x_\alpha(\alpha(t)a)$. These are integral polynomial identities, and do not divide by a factorial in $F$. At zero every root map is the identity.

source.place: Equation (153), p.510; integral coefficient and weight calculations written out.

proof.text: Write $p_\pm$ for the ordered products in the statement. By [lem-sfb-chevalley-unipotent-polynomial-coordinates] they identify affine spaces with closed subgroup schemes $U_\pm$. Choose a rational functional positive on every simple root and separating the finitely many distinct weights: start with the function taking value 1 on every simple root and perturb it within the positive rational cone to avoid the finitely many equations $q(\lambda-\mu)=0$. Ordering weight summands by decreasing $q$ puts $U_+$ in the block upper unitriangular group and $U_-$ in the block lower one. Inside the block diagonal group, $T$ is closed: its coordinate pullback sends a diagonal entry on weight $\lambda$ to $e^\lambda$, an inverse block determinant to $e^{-r_\lambda\lambda}$ where $r_\lambda=\dim W_\lambda$, and off-diagonal entries to zero. Hence it also contains $e^{-\lambda}=e^{-r_\lambda\lambda}(e^\lambda)^{r_\lambda-1}$. Since $\mathbf Z\Omega=P$, these elements generate $F[P]$, so the pullback is surjective.

source.place: Equation (152), p.510; weight-compatible matrix blocks and the explicit weight torus; one-sign collection supplied separately.

proof.text: Apply [lem-sfb-block-gauss-scheme-chart] to these weight blocks. Inside its source, $U_-\times T\times U_+$ is closed: the three coordinate surjections for the closed inclusions tensor to a surjection, so the product is a closed subscheme. Thus its multiplication map $j:C=\mathbf A^N\times T\times\mathbf A^N\to\operatorname{GL}(W_F)$ is a closed immersion into the Gauss open, hence a quasi-compact immersion. Its coordinate algebra is a polynomial algebra over $F[P]$. The finite set $\Omega$ generates $P$ by hypothesis, and $P\subset V$ is torsion-free since $V$ is rational. Hence [lem-trf-fg-torsionfree-group-free] gives a finite basis of $P$, making $F[P]$ a Laurent polynomial algebra. Consequently both $C$ and $C\times_F C$ are integral. The coordinate origin with middle factor 1 maps to the identity.

source.place: Theorem 23.72, pp.510-511; agent Gauss-chart immersion argument, with the general matrix chart stated separately.

proof.text: [lem-sfb-chevalley-opposite-rational-collection] writes $v_1u_2=u_0t_0v_0$ on an open neighbourhood of $(1,1)$ in $U_+\times U_-$, with $u_i\in U_-$, $v_i\in U_+$ and $t_i\in T$. Thus on a nonempty open of $C\times C$ the product of $u_1t_1v_1$ and $u_2t_2v_2$ equals $[u_1(t_1u_0t_1^{-1})](t_1t_0t_2)[(t_2^{-1}v_0t_2)v_2]$, a morphism into $C$. The brackets lie in $U_-$ and $U_+$, respectively, by their subgroup property and the conjugation formula of step 1. For inversion, apply the same collection identity to $v^{-1}(t^{-1}u^{-1}t)=u_0t_0v_0$; then $(utv)^{-1}=u_0(t_0t^{-1})(tv_0t^{-1})$. Its domain is a nonempty open of $C$, since it contains the identity. Both domains are dense by step 3. This proves generic factorization of multiplication and inversion as morphisms, including their scheme structures.

source.place: Theorem 23.72 omitted details, p.511; agent assembly of localized opposite-product identities, before any reductivity assertion.

proof.text: Apply [lem-sfb-generic-matrix-locus-subgroup-closure] to the immersion $j:C\to\operatorname{GL}(W_F)$. The source is affine of finite type and remains integral over any field extension, since its algebra is polynomial/Laurent polynomial by step 3. The identity point is present. Step 4 gives the required nonempty open domains and actual morphism factorizations of multiplication and inversion. Thus the scheme-theoretic image $H$ of $C$ is a closed subgroup. Every generator $T,x_\alpha$ factors through $C$ by setting the other coordinates to zero, so $K\subseteq H$. Conversely $C$ factors through $K$ by multiplication of these generators; minimality of the scheme-theoretic image gives $H\subseteq K$ [def-nagata-scheme-theoretic-image]. Hence $H=K$ as closed subgroup schemes.

source.place: Theorem 23.72, p.511; agent coordinate-kernel argument. Scheme-theoretic image is used only with its defining minimality and kernel ideal.

proof.text: By [lemma-nagata-immersion-open-in-scheme-image], the quasi-compact immersion $j$ is an open immersion into its scheme-theoretic image $H=K$. Its image contains the identity by step 3. Conjugating each factor using step 1 gives equivariance: $a_\beta\mapsto(-\beta)(t)a_\beta$, $b_\beta\mapsto\beta(t)b_\beta$, and the middle factor is fixed since $T$ is commutative. This identity holds on every test algebra, so it is an identity of morphisms.

source.place: Theorem 23.72, p.511; general immersion/image lemma supplies openness, not a reductive-group big-cell theorem.

proof.text: The tangent space of an open neighbourhood equals that of the ambient scheme at its point. Directly from the product coordinates at $(0,1,0)$, the differential of multiplication is $(a,z,b)\mapsto\sum_\beta a_\beta dx_{-\beta}(1)+z+\sum_\beta b_\beta dx_\beta(1)$: multiply matrices over $F[\epsilon]/(\epsilon^2)$ and discard quadratic terms. It is an isomorphism because step 6 is an open immersion. Differentiating the equivariance identity gives characters $-\beta,0,\beta$ on the corresponding summands. Each root coordinate has a nonzero unit tangent vector, whose image is nonzero under this isomorphism; the characters are distinct as elements of $P$, even if their differentials agree in small characteristic. This gives the asserted tangent direct sum. If $R=\varnothing$, its spanning hypothesis gives $V=P=0$, $T=1$, and both products and the generated group are 1. The displayed morphism is then the identity.
